text:
nina: Vela Systems needs a concise perf POC to close procurement. Scope: streaming chat (1k ctx) + high-ingest embeddings. They want p95 token-stream <= 300ms, sustain 80 qps, microbursts to 320 qps for up to 4 minutes. embeddings 1200 reqs/min, 768-d. can eng propose runbook + quick committed vs burst cost sketch?
ryan: quick clarifiers: model variant = 13B quant? do they want an fp16 baseline for comparison? also want graceful fallback behavior documented?
nina: yes 13B quant first, include an optional FP16 run if we miss SLA. fallback to 7B auto-route is fine. p95 target is hard requirement.
devon: proposed compact runbook (4 phases): smoke, warmup, steady-state, burst cycles. use anonymized sample corpus (avg prompt 140 tokens, gen 220). include a cache-eviction scenario and a cold-start check.
devon: runbook draft:
```
phase 1 - smoke: 3m @ 1-3 qps (auth + shape)
phase 2 - warmup: 15m ramp to 40 qps (populate prefix/KV caches)
phase 3 - sustain: ramp -> hold 80 qps for 30m, collect p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec
phase 4 - bursts: 4 cycles 4m @ 320 qps with 3m cooldowns
extra: cold-start test: terminate one node and issue 12 concurrent streams
metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, gpu_util%, queue_depth, 5xx rate
```
ryan: loadgen tooling: vegeta for high-throughput calls + small node SSE client for streaming. example streaming call: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream`
ryan: infra rough: sustained 80 qps on 13B-quant -> estimated 3 A100-eq GPUs (round to 3 committed units). bursts to 320 qps -> +3 pre-warmed GPUs. recommend commit 3 units and a 3-unit burst cushion.
chloe: ballpark pricing (procurement-friendly): commit 3 units -> ~$75k/month. burst on-demand burn ~ $140/hr per GPU * 3 => $420/hr while active. note: quoting is conservative until we have a profiling run.
sec-bot: security-note: Vela requires customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, per-request audit logs, and SOC2 artifacts. For the POC we can use a temporary key and snapshot logs. will need their security contact and a signed DPA.
nina: henry from Vela is on email; henry can you confirm security lead and whether they require HSM specifically?
chloe: failure modes summary to hand off to their SRE team: cold-start tail latency, KV cache miss storms, ingress fan-in causing queueing, and backend retries amplifying load. mitigations: staged warmup, prefix caching, pre-warm nodes during ramp, rate shaping + circuit-breaker, graceful fallback to 7B variant and explained 503s.
henry (via email): security lead is kate.s@vela.com, they prefer HSM-backed keys but can accept cloud-KMS for POC. questionnaire to follow in ~90m. we'll also need the fallback playbook for our runbook review.
devon: deliverables: CSV with columns: phase,qps,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_s,gpu_util_pct,queue_depth,errors_pct,fallback_events and 1-page exec summary (SLA met? cost implications).
r yan: timeline: run smoke + warmup tomorrow 10:00 PT, full run and initial CSV within 36h. owners: devon (loadgen + results), ryan (infra & cost refinement), sec-bot/chloe (security checklist + temporary KMS).
nina: action items recap: devon (payloads & loadgen), ryan (infra sizing + refined cost after profiling), chloe (security steps), henry (security contact + questionnaire). I'll collate and send to procurement and attach CSV to the deal. :thumbsup:
henry: sending questionnaire and security contact now. thanks team.
nina: thanks all — keep updates here. we'll include the CSV and the 1-pager in the contract annex.
